openings.claim: Can Z1's location checks and movement updates remain complete within the preparation limit without adding service delay for the sole clerk? A ten-minute stopping rule alone does not establish this capability.
openings.delta: Distinguish a complete, affordable record from a budget-compliant but incomplete record before attributing outcomes to address accuracy.
openings.prediction: If record maintenance is the limiting dependency, checks remain unfinished at ten minutes or delayed encounters coincide with update work and missed entries.
openings.rival_prediction: Ordinary queue congestion is the nearest alternative: delays track arrivals even when no checking or updates occur and records remain current.
openings.defeat: Complete checks within ten preparation minutes and consistently current entries maintained without detectable service delay would defeat the workload objection in the sampled conditions.
openings.probe: During unchanged handling, the clerk uses existing paper to note checking duration, unfinished checks, movement entries and coincident delays. Stop preparation at ten minutes; incomplete evidence remains inconclusive.
assumptions: Fit evaluates bounded observation; Z1's intervention and target performance remain unproven.
Recording overhead can remain negligible; otherwise this probe is inconclusive.

openings.claim: Does A1's assumed existing ownership check distinguish the intended reader when storage uses another household member's surname? Stable locations do not establish correct-reader handoff.
openings.delta: Examine the unsupported ownership dependency separately from location consistency.
openings.prediction: If the dependency fails, household-name discrepancies leave ownership unresolved despite a known location.
openings.rival_prediction: Harmless storage aliases are the nearest alternative: the existing check uniquely resolves ownership despite surname discrepancies.
openings.defeat: Existing information and the actual check reliably resolve every sampled discrepant hold's intended reader within the time target.
openings.probe: The existing clerk reviews the current check and records anonymous resolved/unresolved outcomes during unchanged handling, within ten preparation minutes. Keep identities behind the desk; conduct no experimental handoffs.
assumptions: Observation fit does not establish A1 feasibility or zero wrong-reader handoffs.

critiques.issue: Its preservation claim depends on complete maintenance under the clerk's workload; the stopping rule proves only a time ceiling.
Its intervention depends on an ownership check not supplied by the fixture; accurate locations alone cannot verify correctness.
